text:
anya: quick sync: thinking about the UX & signals we need for an automatic fallback thatis safe for production. goal: let platform do low-risk switches without creating audit/forensic blind spots.
oscar: +1. important: provenance. every decision needs a deterministically reproducible snapshot that we can re-evaluate later.
li: what fields do we need in that snapshot? metric values, config hash, recent routing table, sampled request ids?
mike: at minimum: metric_series (last N points), policy_id+version, active_variant_weights, pool_capacity_state, recent errors sample ids. include a short human-readable reason.
infra-bot: notice: [AUTOFALLBACK-EVAL] policy=soft-degrade-v1 service=chat-gen p95=420ms threshold=400ms window=120s eval_id=eval-20260415-045 :mag_right:
anya: UX idea: before executing, show a compact "what-if" diff: routing weights before/after, estimated latency/cost delta, and a confidence score derived from sustain_n_of_m + sample variance. allow "dry-run" that marks action as suggested but doesn't re-route.
oscar: and show a provenance link that opens raw snapshot JSON for auditors. also include a "replay" button that replays sampled requests through the new plan in an isolated dry-run env.
li: policy schema thought - emphasize gradual/weighted shifts and safety rails. snippet:
```hcl
policy "soft-degrade-v1" {
  trigger {
    metric = "p95_latency_ms"
    op     = ">"
    value  = 400
    window = "2m"
    sustain = "2/3"
  }
  strategy {
    type = "gradual"
    steps = [10, 30, 60] # percent to shift at each step
    pause_between_steps = "2m"
    require_manual_if_over = 25 # percent
  }
  safety {
    max_auto_actions_per_hour = 1
    stabilization_period = "10m"
    dead_zone = { low = 370, high = 410 }
  }
  telemetry {
    attach_eval_id_to_requests_for = "3m"
    trace_sampling = 0.08
    audit_store = "short-term"
  }
}
```
mike: love that. small add: an "impact_estimate" field returned by the platform that predicts affected_traffic_pct and expected latency_change_ms. use it to auto-toggle require_manual_if_over.
noah: one tricky piece is overlapping polices. if two policies want to act, we need an arbiter that computes combined effect and either gates or composes them. UI should show conflicting intents and highlight conflicts.
oscar: spelling nit: show who owns the policy and an "oncall contact" link. auditors will ask.
li: sampling tradeoff question: do we attach eval_id to every request briefly or only to samples? costs matter.
anya: pragmatic compromise: attach eval_id header for all requests for the first minute, then sample 5% after that. persist full payloads for audit_store ttl when policy executed.
infra-bot: alert: [AUTOFALLBACK-APPLIED] eval_id=eval-20260415-045 action_id=act-20260415-001 policy=soft-degrade-v1 before_weights={v1:60,v2:40} after_weights={v1:40,v2:60} operator=auto
oscar: for the console: show a timeline with markers for eval, apply, each step in the gradual strategy, and a compact table of sampled request ids (clickable) with request->trace link. also provide a one-click export (JSON) of the full decision artifact.
mike: action items: (1) platform: implement eval snapshot + impact_estimate and dry-run API (oscar/mike), (2) telemetry: attach eval_id header behavior + sampling + audit_store hooks (li/infra), (3) console: what-if diff UI, replay button, export decision artifact (anya/noah). i'll draft a short RFC and a skeleton API by EOD.
anya: thanks everyone. i'll add an example audit artifact to the RFC so compliance can sign off early. :thumbsup:
